author: GPT-6 (Codex)
status: Subjective scenario prior, specified before computing its resulting stopping quantiles. Not an empirically estimated posterior.
target: Distribution of the globally optimal realized stopping point conditional on each deterministic law; not a Bayes-optimal adaptive policy.

log10_H.note: Illustrative finite-ceiling headroom of10 to1e12; no empirical or physical bound establishes this range. Sensitivity uses max3,30,120.

single_power_gap.note: Factor3 one-standard-deviation uncertainty around a weak p=.5 center; search/adaptive mechanisms justify broad uncertainty, not these exact probabilities.

heterogeneous_gaps.note: A weak residual bottleneck atop faster bulk improvements; amplitude and exponent ranges are judgmental. Both receive the same universal multiplier.

rapid_ceiling.note: Represents efficient adaptive refinement or discrete exhaustion; no tail exponent is fitted.

continuous_slow_gaps.cost_gap: integral from p=0 to1 of(1+F/F0)^(-p) dp
continuous_slow_gaps.note: Stylized hierarchy of increasingly hard refinements; finite ceiling can remain irrelevant during the budget.

scale_free_within_budget.note: Descriptive raw-input law over the available budget; need not assert literal infinite headroom beyond it. Roughly covers empirical finite-range exponents.

rationale: Finite ceilings are plausible but not implied by a finite raw budget or by an unspecified universal thought unit.
Give heterogeneous residual bottlenecks more weight than a single cost-gap exponent because broad cognitive efficiency plausibly depends on multiple improvable mechanisms.
Retain substantial rapid-convergence weight because adaptive optimization and finite discrete opportunities can improve much faster than random search.
Retain substantial very-slow or effectively scale-free weight because small-amplitude difficult opportunities can matter at a1e-120 marginal threshold.
Do not count correlated empirical fits as independent evidence or use their count to set family weights.
Weights deliberately expose subjective judgment. Sensitivity across reasonable alternative weights is more informative than Monte Carlo sampling error.
